newsitem.title: USA: ABB nuclear blueprint wins U.S. approval.
newsitem.headline: ABB nuclear blueprint wins U.S. approval.

text.p: ABB Inc, a unit of ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, on Thursday said the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) certified its blueprint for a standard nuclear power plant, which could reduce construction delays and costs.
ABB's System 80+ Standard Plant is an advanced light-water reactor developed by ABB, the U.S. Department of Energy, Stone & Webster Inc and Duke Engineering & Services, ABB said.
The certification means that a U.S. owner can obtain a single NRC license in one step to both build and operate the plant, before construction begins, ABB said.
ABB said the renewable, 15-year certification could avert costly design changes, which caused higher construction costs of most nuclear units built in the 1970s and 1980s.
The design certification culminates a $100 million design and licensing effort that spanned more than 10 years, ABB said.
In a separate statement, ABB Inc said it entered into three agreements with Korea Electric Power Corp for ABB to continue to support the Korean nuclear power program for the next 10 years.
